note: Codes: data/mexico_2025_safety.do (Bookmark #14, Q4 2025 Public Safety Perception; exports mexico_2025_q4safety_perception.csv, line 823) keeps the 53 INEGI columns bp1_1..bp1_9_6 from conjunto_de_datos_ensu_cb_1225.csv (import delimited case(lower); id = _n within 2025 Q4), keep list identical to Q2 2025's Bookmark #5 (incl. bp1_6_1..bp1_6_8), and reshapes long with item = column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no positional step). Recodes: 9 -> missing on every bp1_*; 3 (No aplica) -> missing on bp1_2_*, bp1_5_*, bp1_7_*. mapping_basis=data_labels: INEGI's 1225 data dictionary labels every BP1_* column (e.g. BP1_2_03 'Percepcion de seguridad en la calle'; BP1_2_12 '...en el parque o centro recreativo'; BP1_5_4 '...permitir que los (las) menores de edad que viven en el hogar salgan solos(as) por temor a sufrir algun delito'; BP1_6_6 'Victima perteneciente al hogar de extorsion'; BP1_6_7 '...de fraude bancario'; BP1_9_5 'Percepcion del grado de confianza en la Fuerza Aerea Mexicana'); 53/53 labels name the same place/situation/authority as the Q4 questionnaire sub-item/row carrying the same number, and 132/132 shipped option_text values are character-identical to the 1225 catalogos/<item>.csv label for that code. Dictionary diff 0625 vs 1225 over BP1_*: only BP1_2_03 and BP1_2_12 labels change (now matching the print's 'la calle' / 'parque o centro recreativo'); the 53 catalogos/bp1_*.csv are byte-identical to 0625 after line-ending normalisation. Step 3b, 2025 Q4 vs 2025 Q2 (batch_696) and 2025 Q3 (batch_700), from pdftotext -raw of trim4/trim2/trim3 pp.2-3 diffed word by word, plus 110-dpi renders of trim4 pp.2-3 and 300-dpi crops of the two changed spots read: 2025 Q4 Section I is the Q2/Q4 form -- 1.6 is household victimization over Tarjeta-A incidences 1-8 (bp1_6_1..8, 1=Si/2=No/9), not Q3's news-source checklist (bp1_6_01..13,99). Versus 2025 Q2, two shipped strings change: (a) 1.6 row 6 (bp1_6_6): 'Amenazas, presiones o engaños para exigirle dinero o bienes; ...(extorsion)' -> 'Presiones, engaños o advertencias para exigirle dinero o bienes; o para que hiciera algo o dejara de hacerlo (extorsion)' ('Amenazas' dropped, 'advertencias' added; the 1225 dictionary label 'extorsion' is unchanged); (b) 1.2 stem: the trailing period is gone ('...se siente seguro(a) o inseguro(a)'; Q2 and Q3 print '...inseguro(a).'). Everything else shipped is string-identical to 2025 Q2 after whitespace/dot-leader normalisation, including the reworded 1.2 options 03 'la calle' and 12 'el parque o centro recreativo (lugar fisico publico con areas verdes, ...)' first printed in 2025 Q2, and bp1_5_4 'permitir que los (las) menores de edad que viven en el hogar salgan solos(as)?'. Print-only differences vs Q2, all in stripped interviewer text: 1.7 reinstates 'EL CODIGO 3 "NO APLICA" SOLO SE ACEPTA PARA LA POLICIA PREVENTIVA MUNICIPAL' (as Q3) and the skip note loses its final period; 'APLIQUE 1.8 Y 1.9 PARA CADA CODIGO 1 REGISTRADO EN 1.7' moves position in the text layer; 1.9's code-9 label reads 'Nosabe/noresponde' in the text layer only (a kerning artifact; the render shows 'No sabe / no responde'; code 9 is not shipped). The two 1.6 scope directions are unchanged from Q2. Versus 2025 Q3: 1.6 block differs as above; 1.1-1.5 and 1.7-1.9 shipped strings identical except the 1.2 stem period. Words: text_source=study_materials, the administered 2025 Q4 questionnaire wording (not the terser dictionary labels): all 68 distinct Spanish strings shipped are exact substrings of pdftotext -raw output of trim4 pp.2-3 after whitespace/dot-leader normalisation. File = batch_696's with table/section_id/instrument ('segundo' -> 'cuarto trimestre') and the two changes above; diffed programmatically, nothing else differs (build script .cache/mexico_2025_q4safety_perception/build.R). Structure and conventions identical to batch_679/688/696: CP1 read-aloud intro in instructions; one section_id per question 1.1-1.9; for 1.2 and 1.4-1.9 the stem is in section_prompt and the sub-item/row in item_text; 1.1 and 1.3 single items with the stem in item_text. Kept as printed: (LUGAR)/(CIUDAD)/(AUTORIDAD)/(CODIGO DE LA INCIDENCIA), la (al)/la (del)/la (el), gender fills, trailing '?' and '...', 1.1/1.3 options with trailing '?', '[CDMX (3)]' on bp1_7_1, 'Otro' write-in row (bp1_5_5) as the bare word. Normalised: line wraps joined. Stripped: numbers, dot leaders, entry boxes, write-in lines, ESPECIFIQUE, interviewer directions (CIRCULE UN SOLO CODIGO; REGISTRE EL CODIGO...; MUESTRE LA TARJETA 'A' Y REGISTRE...; PASE AL SIGUIENTE RENGLON; the 1.7 No-aplica and all-2/3/9 skip notes; APLIQUE 1.8 Y 1.9...; the 1.6 scope directions 'PARA LOS CODIGOS DE DELITO 1 Y 2 UNICAMENTE SE DEBERA CONSIDERAR AQUELLOS VEHICULOS QUE SON PROPIEDAD DEL HOGAR' and 'PARA LOS CODIGOS DE DELITO 4, 5, 6, 7 Y 8 UNICAMENTE SE DEBERA CONSIDERAR A LAS PERSONAS INTEGRANTES DEL HOGAR DE 18 ANOS Y MAS' -- disclosed in public_note). Tarjeta A is not in the questionnaire zip; 1.6 item_text is the printed questionnaire row. Options: only levels present in the live data get rows (no 3 No aplica / 9 No sabe rows; set missing by the .do); 132/132 live item x level cells have an option row, 0 extra. Cross-check (route 9 style, .cache/mexico_2025_q4safety_perception/counts.py vs live_counts.csv from a server-side GROUP BY item,resp; no export): raw 1225 CSV 23,923 rows; .do-expected long rows 1,117,773; live COUNT(*) 1,117,773 over 23,923 distinct ids (1..23923 as strings), 0 missing resp, 0 duplicate id x item -- NOT truncated (cf. 2025 Q1's 1,048,575-row cut, batch_692). 132/132 item x level counts identical, e.g. bp1_1 1/2 = 9369/14477 (9=77), bp1_2_03 1/2 = 8837/14776 (3=284, 9=26), bp1_2_04 1/2 = 1214/242 (3=22293, 9=174), bp1_3 1..4 = 5695/4255/7597/6084 (9=292), bp1_5_4 1/2 = 6584/11298 (3=6020, 9=21), bp1_6_6 1/2 = 3246/20668 (9=9), bp1_6_7 1/2 = 1636/22271, bp1_9_1 1..4 = 1154/6369/4194/3431. Id alignment: per-item SUM(id*(resp+1)) server-side equals the raw file with id = row index for 53/53 items. bp1_8_k/bp1_9_k blank in raw exactly where bp1_7_k != 1 (blanks 8712/4930/2815/2365/11696/6268; 0 blanks with bp1_7_k == 1). Dictionary defects: Reference names 'ENSU 2023' while data and wording are the 2025 Q4 wave (file suffix 1225) -- same as the siblings; Description ('Urban safety perception ratings across Mexican cities, Q4 2025') does not mention that 1.6 is household crime victimization. INEGI's 1225 BP1_6_4 and BP1_6_6 labels carry trailing spaces (cosmetic). English in _translated is this project's own translation (machine_translation): reused verbatim from batch_696 (2025 Q2) for every string whose Spanish is identical (130 of 132 rows' item_text_translated, all option/instructions English); fresh only for bp1_6_6 item_text_translated ('Pressure, deception or warnings to demand money or goods from you, or to make you do or stop doing something (extortion)'; 2 rows), and the 1.2 section_prompt_translated had its trailing period dropped to mirror the Spanish (24 rows; wording otherwise batch_696's). INEGI publishes no English questionnaire.
public_note: Fuente: INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Seguridad Pública Urbana (ENSU) 2025, cuarto trimestre -- IRW transcribed Section I (questions 1.1-1.9) from INEGI's questionnaire, stripped interviewer directions (including the 1.6 notes limiting vehicle thefts to household-owned vehicles and incidents 4-8 to household members aged 18+), and added an English translation of its own; INEGI does not endorse this item text. In this quarter the extortion incidence (bp1_6_6) reads 'Presiones, engaños o advertencias' where the 2024 fourth-quarter and 2025 second-quarter tables read 'Amenazas, presiones o engaños', and question 1.2 asks about 'la calle' (bp1_2_03) and a defined 'parque o centro recreativo' (bp1_2_12), unlike the 2024 tables.
